samples.xml_description:
<module id="pulse_detect">
    <description>Implement a module for pulse detection. The 1-bit input signal data_in is a continuous input, which is triggered by clk. When "data_in" changes from 0 to 1 to 0(3 cycles), this is considered as a "pulse". The indicating signal data_out is 1 at the end cycle of the "pulse", and then returns to 0 until the corresponding pulse appears again. For example, if data_in is 01010(5 cycles), the data_out is 00101.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="data_in">One-bit input signal.</input>
        <output id="data_out">Output signal indicating the presence of pulses.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="s0" value="0">Initial state. A state waiting for pulse 0.</parameter>
        <parameter id="s1" value="1">A state waiting for pulse 1.</parameter>
        <parameter id="s2" value="2">A state waiting for pulse 0.</parameter>
        <parameter id="s3" value="3">A state waiting for pulse 1.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <description>
            Notice that below descriptions are along with tags <![CDATA[ <logic />]]>.
            With a <![CDATA[ <logic type="combinational_logic" />]]>, must construct this logic as interal wire declaration. Or this <![CDATA[ <logic type="combinational_logic" />]]> can be declared as a `reg` but only be used in always(*) block.
            With a <![CDATA[ <logic type="sequential_logic" />]]>, must construct this logic as `reg` declaration. Must update this logic, in an always block, based on other <![CDATA[ <logic type="sequential_logic" />]]> or <![CDATA[ <logic type="combinational_logic" />]]> states.
            With a <![CDATA[ <logic type="sequential_logic_operation" />]]>, no declaration for this keyword. Just place this operation sequence in below mentioned description.
            With a <![CDATA[ <logic type="combinational_logic_operation" />]]>, no declaration for this keyword. Just based on the keyword `assign` to construct description of this combinational logic operation.
        </description>
        <logic type="combinational_logic" id="data_out">
        In the reset condition (~rst_n), set the state register to the initial state and set the data_out output to 0, indicating no pulse. Otherwise, the indicating signal data_out is 1 if `pulse_level2` reaches `s2` and `data_in` is 0. Otherwise, returns to 0 until the corresponding pulse appears again. 
        </logic>
        <logic type="sequential_logic" id="pulse_level1">
        If `rst_n` is inactive, `pulse_level1` is reset to 0. Otherwise, `pulse_level1` is set to `pulse_level2`.
        </logic>
        <logic type="combinational_logic" id="pulse_level2">
        In case `pulse_level1` is `s0`, if `data_in` is 0, `pulse_level2` is set to `s1`, else `pulse_level2` is set to `s0`. In case `pulse_level1` is `s1`, if `data_in` is 1, `pulse_level2` is set to `s2`, else `pulse_level2` is set to `s1`. In case `pulse_level1` is `s2`, if `data_in` is 0, `pulse_level2` is set to `s3`, else `pulse_level2` is set to `s0`. In case `pulse_level1` is `s3`, if `data_in` is 1, `pulse_level2` is set to `s2`, else `pulse_level2` is set to `s1`.
        </logic>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>Declare the module pulse_detect with input and output ports as specified in the ports statement.
Declare a register state `pulse_level1` to keep track of the current state of the pulse detection process `pulse_level2`.
</implementation>
</module>
